newsitem.title: SPAIN: ALBANIAN SOCCER PLAYERS ASK SPAIN FOR ASYLUM.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIAN SOCCER PLAYERS ASK SPAIN FOR ASYLUM.

text.p: Seven players and a trainer for Albania's under-21 soccer squad abandoned their team in Madrid on Thursday and asked Spain for asylum, government officials said.

The eight were due to leave for Tirana after two matches in southern Spain but did not get on a flight with the rest of the team at Madrid's airport. They were taken away in a police bus, witnesses said.
The rest of the under-21 team boarded a flight to Athens en route to Albania, which has been rocked by widespread civil strife bordering on anarchy.
Under Spanish law, the government has three months to award or deny asylum, but the Interior Ministry said it would make a prompt decision.
"We intend to solve this in a short period of time, perhaps in one week," Jose Ramon Onega, general director of interior policy at the Interior Ministry, told Reuters.
He said another player had also asked for asylum but backed out at the last minute. "Nine asked for asylum, but one gave up for personal reasons. He said he was going to go to Germany," he said.
A team coach said earlier that two other under-21 players had already left the team in Spain and were heading for Germany with hopes of playing in Frankfurt.
The Albanian national and under-21 teams played matches in or near the southern Spanish city of Granada during the past week after political violence forced the games to be moved from home venues.

The national team, which played World Cup European group qualifying matches in Granada against Ukraine and Germany, was drawn from Albanians playing for clubs outside their own country. The under-21 squad was assembled from teams in the Albanian soccer league.
Under-21 coach Suleiman Mema said some members of the team wanted to stay in Spain to play soccer, even for third or fourth division teams.
"If Spanish authorities decide (to give them asylum) they will be doing an incredible thing for them," he told Reuters. "They will find another life here. They are all young."
Spanish authorities can award asylum in cases of political, racial or religious persecution. But authorities could also allow the eight Albanians to stay for humanitarian reasons, Onega said.
A second under-21 coach, Bashkim Koka, said the players would ask to stay in Spain for two to three months in hopes of getting offers to play locally.
Two of the under-21 players who did board the flight from Madrid, Erion Bogdani and Arian Bezay, said they planned to ask Albania for visas to play in Switzerland.
"For the time being, it is difficult to play in Albania," said Mema, adding he too would have asked for asylum if he did not have a family waiting at home.
"I would like to do the same but I have a family. I've got kids. I have a young wife and I want to go back soon," he said.
The under-21 team fared poorly in the Spanish matches, losing 0-3 to Ukraine last Saturday and 0-4 to Germany on Tuesday.
